newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate climbs 20 bps to 11.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate climbs 20 bps to 11.4 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate climbed 20 basis points to 11.4 percent on Tuesday despite cuts in some interbank rates thanks to weaker demand.
Trade totalled 51 million kuna, of which a little more than a half were new borrowings. Supply stood at 60 million kuna.

Creditors agreed to turn some of the previous call money loans into one- and two-month placements they were reluctant to make during a recent liquidity crisis, boosting the share of the day's term loans to 60 percent.
One-month price fell to 13 percent from 14 and 15 percent and two-month loans were granted at a lower 16 percent.
Banks also charged a lower 11 percent for two-week kuna.
The weighted call money rate eased to 9.5 from 9.9 percent after a mixed trade at 10 percent for interbank loans and nine, charged by insurance firms.
The banks ended Monday with 676 million kuna on their balances and repaid all but 86.15 million kuna in central bank's Lombard loans this morning.
As the overall banking deposits grew, Monday's mandatory reserve payment was also slightly higher at 3.5 billion kuna.
The central bank's kuna mid-rates for Wednesday firmed to 6.1555 against the dollar while easing to 3.5711 to the mark.
